question: Which set of details does a CMOM program record for each sanitary sewer overflow event?
correctAnswer: Date, location, estimated volume, cause and response actions
explanation: Overflow records capture when and where the event happened, how much escaped, why it happened and how crews responded, so the utility can track trends and report events.
options: Crew size, truck number, fuel used and weather noted at the scene
Date, location, estimated volume, cause and response actions
Pipe age, pipe material, soil type and depth of cover at the site
Caller name, billing account, complaint time and follow up result
optionA: Crew size, truck number, fuel used and weather noted at the scene
optionB: Date, location, estimated volume, cause and response actions
optionC: Pipe age, pipe material, soil type and depth of cover at the site
optionD: Caller name, billing account, complaint time and follow up result
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: CMOM Program Development.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: CMOM Program Development

question: A risk based condition assessment program ranks each pipe segment by combining its likelihood of failure with which second factor?
correctAnswer: Consequence of failure for nearby services, roads and waterways
explanation: Risk based ranking pairs how likely a segment is to fail with what happens if it does, so limited inspection funds go to the segments that matter most.
options: Consequence of failure for nearby services, roads and waterways
Distance from the segment to the utility maintenance yard gate
Number of years since the segment was last plotted on a map set
Total length of all segments inspected during the previous year
optionA: Consequence of failure for nearby services, roads and waterways
optionB: Distance from the segment to the utility maintenance yard gate
optionC: Number of years since the segment was last plotted on a map set
optionD: Total length of all segments inspected during the previous year
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Condition Assessment Programs.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: Condition Assessment Programs

question: During a CCTV inspection, the operator logs a fracture defect in a clay pipe. Which feature separates a fracture from a simple crack?
correctAnswer: The wall pieces are visibly displaced or starting to separate
explanation: A crack is a visible line with the wall still in place. A fracture goes further, with pieces displaced or separating, which means the wall is breaking apart.
options: The line is visible but the wall pieces remain in their place
The wall pieces are visibly displaced or starting to separate
The defect runs around a joint and follows the joint all the way
Water weeps through the line during a period of dry weather flow
optionA: The line is visible but the wall pieces remain in their place
optionB: The wall pieces are visibly displaced or starting to separate
optionC: The defect runs around a joint and follows the joint all the way
optionD: Water weeps through the line during a period of dry weather flow
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: CCTV Defect Interpretation.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: CCTV Defect Interpretation

question: An inspector wants to find where rainwater can pour into a manhole from the street surface. Which part of the structure does the inspector examine first?
correctAnswer: The frame and cover, including how the cover seats and seals
explanation: Rainwater enters at the top of the structure, so the frame and cover and the way the cover seats are the first places to check for a surface inflow path.
options: The frame and cover, including how the cover seats and seals
The benching at the base, where flow is shaped into the channel
The step irons on the wall, where corrosion weakens climbing aids
The drop pipe at the inlet, where flow falls from a higher sewer
optionA: The frame and cover, including how the cover seats and seals
optionB: The benching at the base, where flow is shaped into the channel
optionC: The step irons on the wall, where corrosion weakens climbing aids
optionD: The drop pipe at the inlet, where flow falls from a higher sewer
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Manhole Assessment.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: Manhole Assessment

question: Which step comes immediately before a resin saturated CIPP liner is cured inside a host pipe?
correctAnswer: The liner is placed inside the host pipe and inflated against its wall
explanation: The liner must be positioned inside the host pipe and held against the wall by pressure before curing starts, so the resin can harden in the right shape and place.
options: The liner is cut open at each lateral and the openings are sealed up
The finished liner is inspected by CCTV and the video record is coded for defects
The liner is placed inside the host pipe and inflated against its wall
The host pipe is lined a second time to build up the wall thickness
optionA: The liner is cut open at each lateral and the openings are sealed up
optionB: The finished liner is inspected by CCTV and the video record is coded for defects
optionC: The liner is placed inside the host pipe and inflated against its wall
optionD: The host pipe is lined a second time to build up the wall thickness
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Rehabilitation Methods CIPP.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Components: Rehabilitation Methods CIPP

question: In slip lining, how does the new carrier pipe get into the existing host pipe?
correctAnswer: It is pulled or pushed through the host pipe and the annular gap is grouted
explanation: Slip lining inserts a smaller prefabricated pipe into the host pipe and grouts the annular gap between them, which is different from bursting or coating methods.
options: It is expanded by a bursting head that breaks the host pipe apart in place
It is folded into a flat shape, pulled in, then rounded out with pressure
It is sprayed onto the host pipe wall in layers until the coating builds up
It is pulled or pushed through the host pipe and the annular gap is grouted
optionA: It is expanded by a bursting head that breaks the host pipe apart in place
optionB: It is folded into a flat shape, pulled in, then rounded out with pressure
optionC: It is sprayed onto the host pipe wall in layers until the coating builds up
optionD: It is pulled or pushed through the host pipe and the annular gap is grouted
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Pipe Bursting And Slip Lining.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Components: Pipe Bursting And Slip Lining

question: Which pair of measurements does a typical area velocity flow monitor record at a manhole?
correctAnswer: Flow depth and flow velocity, combined to calculate the flow rate
explanation: Open channel monitors pair a depth reading with a velocity reading. Multiplying velocity by the flow area from the depth gives the flow rate.
options: Water temperature and air temperature, combined to estimate losses
Flow depth and flow velocity, combined to calculate the flow rate
Pipe diameter and pipe slope, combined to set the camera travel speed
Dissolved oxygen and acidity, combined to grade the sewage strength
optionA: Water temperature and air temperature, combined to estimate losses
optionB: Flow depth and flow velocity, combined to calculate the flow rate
optionC: Pipe diameter and pipe slope, combined to set the camera travel speed
optionD: Dissolved oxygen and acidity, combined to grade the sewage strength
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Flow Monitoring Analysis.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: Flow Monitoring Analysis

question: Which flow pattern in a monitored basin points most directly to rainfall dependent inflow and infiltration?
correctAnswer: Flow rises sharply during and shortly after rain, then falls back toward the dry weather pattern
explanation: A sharp rise tied to rainfall, followed by a return to the normal pattern, is the signature of rainfall dependent inflow and infiltration rather than steady sanitary or groundwater flow.
options: Flow stays almost flat through the whole week, including weekends, holidays and shift changes
Flow climbs slowly over several dry months as the groundwater table rises around the pipes
Flow rises sharply during and shortly after rain, then falls back toward the dry weather pattern
Flow peaks at the same clock times every day no matter what weather passes over the basin
optionA: Flow stays almost flat through the whole week, including weekends, holidays and shift changes
optionB: Flow climbs slowly over several dry months as the groundwater table rises around the pipes
optionC: Flow rises sharply during and shortly after rain, then falls back toward the dry weather pattern
optionD: Flow peaks at the same clock times every day no matter what weather passes over the basin
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Rainfall Dependent I&I.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: Rainfall Dependent I&I

question: Which document in a CMOM program sets out the steps crews follow when sewage overflows from the collection system?
correctAnswer: The overflow response plan the utility keeps for its collection system
explanation: The overflow response plan is the document that lays out notification, containment, cleanup and reporting steps for overflow events in the collection system.
options: The overflow response plan the utility keeps for its collection system
The annual paving schedule the roads department keeps for resurfacing
The water quality file the treatment plant laboratory keeps for testing
The equipment warranty file the supplier keeps for the jetting trucks
optionA: The overflow response plan the utility keeps for its collection system
optionB: The annual paving schedule the roads department keeps for resurfacing
optionC: The water quality file the treatment plant laboratory keeps for testing
optionD: The equipment warranty file the supplier keeps for the jetting trucks
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: CMOM Program Development.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: CMOM Program Development

question: Which result does a utility record for each pipe segment at the end of a condition assessment?
correctAnswer: A condition grade or rating that can be compared across the whole system
explanation: A standard grade lets the utility compare segments across the system and rank them for cleaning, repair or rehabilitation in later program steps.
options: A replacement date that stays fixed no matter what later inspections find
A resale value that the segment could be sold for to a neighbouring utility
A flow capacity figure that replaces the need for any further monitoring
A condition grade or rating that can be compared across the whole system
optionA: A replacement date that stays fixed no matter what later inspections find
optionB: A resale value that the segment could be sold for to a neighbouring utility
optionC: A flow capacity figure that replaces the need for any further monitoring
optionD: A condition grade or rating that can be compared across the whole system
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Condition Assessment Programs.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: Condition Assessment Programs

question: A CCTV run shows fine roots entering through several joints in a 200 mm clay sewer, with no cracks or deformation. Which follow up action fits this finding?
correctAnswer: Schedule root treatment and cleaning, then re-inspect the sewer to confirm control
explanation: Fine roots at joints are a maintenance problem first. Cleaning and root treatment, followed by a check inspection, control them without jumping to replacement or lining.
options: Excavate the full length of the sewer and replace it before the next rain event
Line the pipe at once, because root entry at a joint means the pipe has collapsed
Schedule root treatment and cleaning, then re-inspect the sewer to confirm control
Leave the finding alone, because roots at joints have no effect on sewer flow
optionA: Excavate the full length of the sewer and replace it before the next rain event
optionB: Line the pipe at once, because root entry at a joint means the pipe has collapsed
optionC: Schedule root treatment and cleaning, then re-inspect the sewer to confirm control
optionD: Leave the finding alone, because roots at joints have no effect on sewer flow
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: CCTV Defect Interpretation.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: CCTV Defect Interpretation

question: A manhole in a low paved area has a cover sitting below the surrounding surface, and water ponds over it after rain. Which repair best addresses the inflow at this structure?
correctAnswer: Raise and reseal the frame and cover to grade so ponded water stays out
explanation: Ponded water enters through the top of the structure. Raising the frame to grade and sealing the cover removes that entry path, while benching and pipe work do not.
options: Replace the benching inside the manhole so sewage flows faster through it
Raise and reseal the frame and cover to grade so ponded water stays out
Install a larger inlet pipe so the manhole accepts more sewage at peak flow
Coat the inside walls with a lining that resists corrosion from sewer gas
optionA: Replace the benching inside the manhole so sewage flows faster through it
optionB: Raise and reseal the frame and cover to grade so ponded water stays out
optionC: Install a larger inlet pipe so the manhole accepts more sewage at peak flow
optionD: Coat the inside walls with a lining that resists corrosion from sewer gas
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Manhole Assessment.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: Manhole Assessment

question: A 300 mm sewer has cracking and joint infiltration along its length but keeps its round shape and line. The road above cannot be closed for open cut work. Which feature makes CIPP a suitable choice here?
correctAnswer: The liner installs through existing manholes and cures into a new pipe inside the host
explanation: CIPP is installed from existing access points and forms a structural pipe inside the host, which suits a pipe that keeps its shape but leaks at cracks and joints.
options: The liner installs through existing manholes and cures into a new pipe inside the host
The liner makes the pipe so much larger that bypass pumping is not needed during work
The resin dissolves the old pipe during curing so only the new liner stays in the ground
The crew can install the liner without cleaning or inspecting the host pipe beforehand
optionA: The liner installs through existing manholes and cures into a new pipe inside the host
optionB: The liner makes the pipe so much larger that bypass pumping is not needed during work
optionC: The resin dissolves the old pipe during curing so only the new liner stays in the ground
optionD: The crew can install the liner without cleaning or inspecting the host pipe beforehand
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Rehabilitation Methods CIPP.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Components: Rehabilitation Methods CIPP

question: A subdivision sewer must grow from 200 mm to 300 mm on the same alignment, and the surface above is a finished street. Which method can upsize the pipe in place?
correctAnswer: Pipe bursting, which breaks the old pipe outward while pulling the larger new pipe in
explanation: Pipe bursting is the trenchless method that can increase size on the same line, because the old pipe is fractured outward as the larger new pipe is pulled in.
options: Slip lining, which needs a host pipe larger than the new pipe that is installed inside
Spot repair, which patches one short section and leaves the rest of the pipe unchanged
Jet cleaning, which removes deposits so the old pipe returns to its full design size
Pipe bursting, which breaks the old pipe outward while pulling the larger new pipe in
optionA: Slip lining, which needs a host pipe larger than the new pipe that is installed inside
optionB: Spot repair, which patches one short section and leaves the rest of the pipe unchanged
optionC: Jet cleaning, which removes deposits so the old pipe returns to its full design size
optionD: Pipe bursting, which breaks the old pipe outward while pulling the larger new pipe in
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Pipe Bursting And Slip Lining.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Components: Pipe Bursting And Slip Lining

question: A utility monitors two basins of similar size for four dry weeks. Basin A shows a minimum night flow of 4 L/s and Basin B shows 11 L/s. Which conclusion does this comparison support?
correctAnswer: Basin B likely carries more groundwater infiltration and should be investigated first
explanation: High minimum night flow, when residents use little water, points to groundwater entering the pipes. Basin B shows the stronger signal, so it is checked first.
options: Basin A likely serves more people at night because its night flow is the lower of the two
Basin B likely has a blocked trunk sewer because a high night flow signals a blockage
Basin B likely carries more groundwater infiltration and should be investigated first
Both basins carry the same infiltration because both were measured during the night
optionA: Basin A likely serves more people at night because its night flow is the lower of the two
optionB: Basin B likely has a blocked trunk sewer because a high night flow signals a blockage
optionC: Basin B likely carries more groundwater infiltration and should be investigated first
optionD: Both basins carry the same infiltration because both were measured during the night
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Flow Monitoring Analysis.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: Flow Monitoring Analysis

question: After a storm, flow in a basin keeps rising for several hours after the rain stops and takes two days to return to normal. Which RDII source does this slow response point to?
correctAnswer: Rainfall derived infiltration entering through pipe and manhole defects below ground
explanation: A slow rise and a long tail after rain fit infiltration that soaks through the ground and enters defects, while direct inflow sources respond within minutes.
options: Rainfall derived infiltration entering through pipe and manhole defects below ground
Direct inflow from roof leaders connected straight into the sanitary sewer mains
Inflow through cover holes in a flooded street during the peak of the storm
Cross connections from a storm sewer that discharge minutes after rain begins
optionA: Rainfall derived infiltration entering through pipe and manhole defects below ground
optionB: Direct inflow from roof leaders connected straight into the sanitary sewer mains
optionC: Inflow through cover holes in a flooded street during the peak of the storm
optionD: Cross connections from a storm sewer that discharge minutes after rain begins
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Rainfall Dependent I&I.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: Rainfall Dependent I&I

question: Three overflows in one year all trace back to the same grease blocked sewer reach. Under a CMOM approach, which response addresses the pattern rather than only the events?
correctAnswer: Add the reach to a scheduled grease control and cleaning program and track the results
explanation: A CMOM program treats repeat overflows as a program gap, not isolated events. Adding the reach to a tracked grease control and cleaning program attacks the cause.
options: Respond to each overflow the same way as before and close each file once it is cleaned
Add the reach to a scheduled grease control and cleaning program and track the results
Fine the nearest restaurant one time and take no further steps to track grease sources
Wait for a fourth overflow at the reach before deciding whether the pattern needs action
optionA: Respond to each overflow the same way as before and close each file once it is cleaned
optionB: Add the reach to a scheduled grease control and cleaning program and track the results
optionC: Fine the nearest restaurant one time and take no further steps to track grease sources
optionD: Wait for a fourth overflow at the reach before deciding whether the pattern needs action
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: CMOM Program Development.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: CMOM Program Development

question: A utility can inspect only 20 percent of its sewers this year. Which selection approach fits a risk based condition assessment program?
correctAnswer: Inspect the segments with the highest combined likelihood and consequence of failure first
explanation: Risk based programs spend limited inspection budgets where failure is both likely and costly, instead of spreading the work by age, distance or chance.
options: Inspect the newest segments first because their warranty records are still easy to locate
Inspect segments drawn at random from a map so that every street receives an equal chance
Inspect only the segments closest to the yard so that crews spend less time on the road
Inspect the segments with the highest combined likelihood and consequence of failure first
optionA: Inspect the newest segments first because their warranty records are still easy to locate
optionB: Inspect segments drawn at random from a map so that every street receives an equal chance
optionC: Inspect only the segments closest to the yard so that crews spend less time on the road
optionD: Inspect the segments with the highest combined likelihood and consequence of failure first
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Condition Assessment Programs.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: Condition Assessment Programs

question: During a CCTV inspection the camera view is blocked by a heavy grease deposit covering half the pipe diameter. Which step should the operator take before coding the pipe condition?
correctAnswer: Clean the sewer first, then repeat the inspection so the pipe wall can be seen clearly
explanation: Condition coding depends on seeing the pipe wall. Cleaning first and inspecting again gives a record the utility can trust for repair decisions.
options: Clean the sewer first, then repeat the inspection so the pipe wall can be seen clearly
Code the hidden wall as sound, because a grease deposit usually forms on a sound wall
Raise the camera speed so the unit passes the deposit before the view is fully blocked
Report the segment as collapsed, because the camera could not travel past the deposit
optionA: Clean the sewer first, then repeat the inspection so the pipe wall can be seen clearly
optionB: Code the hidden wall as sound, because a grease deposit usually forms on a sound wall
optionC: Raise the camera speed so the unit passes the deposit before the view is fully blocked
optionD: Report the segment as collapsed, because the camera could not travel past the deposit
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: CCTV Defect Interpretation.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: CCTV Defect Interpretation

question: An inspector finds a cracked chimney seal and mineral staining on the manhole wall just below the frame. Which problem do these signs identify?
correctAnswer: Infiltration entering through the chimney section between the frame and the cone
explanation: Staining just below the frame, paired with a cracked chimney seal, shows water entering through the chimney section rather than at the base or the lower barrel.
options: Surcharge pressure forcing sewage outward through the benching at the manhole base
Corrosion of the lowest barrel section caused by sewer gas trapped in the headspace
Infiltration entering through the chimney section between the frame and the cone
Root growth entering through the joints of the lowest section of the manhole barrel
optionA: Surcharge pressure forcing sewage outward through the benching at the manhole base
optionB: Corrosion of the lowest barrel section caused by sewer gas trapped in the headspace
optionC: Infiltration entering through the chimney section between the frame and the cone
optionD: Root growth entering through the joints of the lowest section of the manhole barrel
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Manhole Assessment.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: Manhole Assessment

question: A CIPP liner has cured in a street where six homes connect to the sewer. Which step restores service to those homes after curing?
correctAnswer: A robotic cutter reopens each lateral connection from inside the lined pipe
explanation: Cured CIPP covers the lateral openings. A robotic cutter sent through the lined pipe reopens each connection from inside, with no excavation at each home.
options: Crews excavate each front yard and reconnect the laterals from the outside
A robotic cutter reopens each lateral connection from inside the lined pipe
The liner is pulled back out so workers can mark the lateral openings by hand
Each home is moved onto a new sewer built along the rear of the properties
optionA: Crews excavate each front yard and reconnect the laterals from the outside
optionB: A robotic cutter reopens each lateral connection from inside the lined pipe
optionC: The liner is pulled back out so workers can mark the lateral openings by hand
optionD: Each home is moved onto a new sewer built along the rear of the properties
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Rehabilitation Methods CIPP.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Components: Rehabilitation Methods CIPP

question: A 450 mm host sewer is slip lined with a 375 mm pipe. Residents are told capacity will not drop as much as the size change suggests. Which factor supports that statement?
correctAnswer: The smooth new pipe wall cuts friction losses enough to offset much of the size loss
explanation: The new pipe is smaller, but its smooth wall creates far less friction than the rough old wall, so the flow capacity drops by much less than the diameter change suggests.
options: The grout placed in the annulus carries part of the flow around the outside of the new carrier pipe
The new pipe stretches under flow pressure until it matches the old pipe diameter
The smaller pipe warms the sewage as it passes so the flow moves through more freely
The smooth new pipe wall cuts friction losses enough to offset much of the size loss
optionA: The grout placed in the annulus carries part of the flow around the outside of the new carrier pipe
optionB: The new pipe stretches under flow pressure until it matches the old pipe diameter
optionC: The smaller pipe warms the sewage as it passes so the flow moves through more freely
optionD: The smooth new pipe wall cuts friction losses enough to offset much of the size loss
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Pipe Bursting And Slip Lining.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Components: Pipe Bursting And Slip Lining

question: A flow monitor in a manhole suddenly reports flows 30 percent higher than the week before, with no rain and no change reported by the pump station downstream. Which check comes first?
correctAnswer: Verify the depth sensor reading against a manual depth measurement taken in the manhole
explanation: A sudden jump with no matching change downstream suggests a measurement problem first. Checking the sensor against a hand measured depth confirms or clears the data.
options: Verify the depth sensor reading against a manual depth measurement taken in the manhole
Assume a new subdivision connected overnight and revise the basin design flows at once
Replace the downstream pump, because its operating records disagree with the monitor
End the basin study, because the data set now clearly contains an error in the records
optionA: Verify the depth sensor reading against a manual depth measurement taken in the manhole
optionB: Assume a new subdivision connected overnight and revise the basin design flows at once
optionC: Replace the downstream pump, because its operating records disagree with the monitor
optionD: End the basin study, because the data set now clearly contains an error in the records
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Flow Monitoring Analysis.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: Flow Monitoring Analysis

question: A basin study shows a fast RDII response. The utility wants to find roof leaders and area drains tied into the sanitary sewer. Which field method targets those direct connections?
correctAnswer: Dye testing of suspect roof leaders and drains while crews watch the sanitary manhole
explanation: Dye testing traces a specific property connection. Dye poured into a suspect leader or drain appears in the sanitary manhole only if that connection exists.
options: Night flow monitoring over four dry weeks at the outlet manhole of the study basin
CCTV inspection of the trunk sewer during a dry weather period of low sewage flow
Dye testing of suspect roof leaders and drains while crews watch the sanitary manhole
Flow isolation with plugs moved from manhole to manhole through the basin at night
optionA: Night flow monitoring over four dry weeks at the outlet manhole of the study basin
optionB: CCTV inspection of the trunk sewer during a dry weather period of low sewage flow
optionC: Dye testing of suspect roof leaders and drains while crews watch the sanitary manhole
optionD: Flow isolation with plugs moved from manhole to manhole through the basin at night
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Rainfall Dependent I&I.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: Rainfall Dependent I&I

question: A developer asks to connect a new subdivision to a sewer reach that already surcharges in heavy rain. Which CMOM capacity step should the utility complete before approving the connection?
correctAnswer: Assess the remaining wet weather capacity of the reach and set approval conditions from the results
explanation: Capacity assurance means checking that a reach can carry added wet weather flow before new connections are approved, and setting conditions when capacity is tight.
options: Approve the connection and place the reach on the inspection list for the following budget year
Assess the remaining wet weather capacity of the reach and set approval conditions from the results
Ask the developer to promise that future residents will use less water during heavy rain events
Connect the subdivision at the nearest manhole and record the added flow after the first year
optionA: Approve the connection and place the reach on the inspection list for the following budget year
optionB: Assess the remaining wet weather capacity of the reach and set approval conditions from the results
optionC: Ask the developer to promise that future residents will use less water during heavy rain events
optionD: Connect the subdivision at the nearest manhole and record the added flow after the first year
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: CMOM Program Development.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: CMOM Program Development

question: Two sewers are the same age. Segment X has a grade 5 structural defect and Segment Y has grade 2 defects. Which scheduling decision follows from the condition data?
correctAnswer: Move Segment X ahead of Segment Y in the rehabilitation program even though their ages match
explanation: Condition data, not age alone, drives rehabilitation order. A grade 5 structural defect outranks a grade 2 defect even when both pipes were installed in the same year.
options: Keep both segments in age order, because condition grades do not change rehabilitation priority
Rehabilitate Segment Y first, because its lower grade repairs cost less in the current season
Postpone both segments until they reach the standard age used for the rest of the program
Move Segment X ahead of Segment Y in the rehabilitation program even though their ages match
optionA: Keep both segments in age order, because condition grades do not change rehabilitation priority
optionB: Rehabilitate Segment Y first, because its lower grade repairs cost less in the current season
optionC: Postpone both segments until they reach the standard age used for the rest of the program
optionD: Move Segment X ahead of Segment Y in the rehabilitation program even though their ages match
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Condition Assessment Programs.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: Condition Assessment Programs

question: A CCTV video shows the camera passing through standing water in a mid section of pipe while the sections before and after run dry at low flow. Which defect should the operator log for the wet section?
correctAnswer: A sag in the pipe grade that ponds water in the low section between events
explanation: Standing water in one section at low flow means the grade dips there. That low spot is a sag, which collects water and solids between flow events.
options: A sag in the pipe grade that ponds water in the low section between events
An offset joint where one pipe end sits higher than the pipe end beside it
A protruding lateral that sticks out into the flow from the side pipe wall
Surface damage where the inner wall has worn away along the pipe invert
optionA: A sag in the pipe grade that ponds water in the low section between events
optionB: An offset joint where one pipe end sits higher than the pipe end beside it
optionC: A protruding lateral that sticks out into the flow from the side pipe wall
optionD: Surface damage where the inner wall has worn away along the pipe invert
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: CCTV Defect Interpretation.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: CCTV Defect Interpretation

question: A manhole beside a creek has open pick holes in its cover, and the creek rises over the cover during spring melt. Which low cost change cuts this inflow source?
correctAnswer: Fit a gasketed, watertight cover with sealed holes on that manhole
explanation: The inflow path is the cover itself when creek water rises over it. A sealed, gasketed cover closes the holes and the seating gap that let the water in.
options: Enlarge the holes so creek water drains back out of the manhole
Remove the cover during spring melt so water can flow more freely
Fit a gasketed, watertight cover with sealed holes on that manhole
Lower the manhole frame so the cover sits below the level of the bank
optionA: Enlarge the holes so creek water drains back out of the manhole
optionB: Remove the cover during spring melt so water can flow more freely
optionC: Fit a gasketed, watertight cover with sealed holes on that manhole
optionD: Lower the manhole frame so the cover sits below the level of the bank
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Manhole Assessment.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Monitoring & Evaluation: Manhole Assessment

question: Before a CIPP crew inverts a liner on a live sewer, which preparation keeps sewage from backing up into homes during the cure?
correctAnswer: Set up bypass pumping sized for the expected flow for the installation and cure period
explanation: While a liner is placed and cured, the sewer cannot carry its normal flow. Bypass pumping sized for that flow protects homes from backups during the work.
options: Ask residents to run extra water so the flow pushes the liner into place more evenly
Set up bypass pumping sized for the expected flow for the installation and cure period
Seal every manhole upstream and let the sewage pond on the street surface overnight
Speed up the cure so bypass equipment is only needed for the first few minutes of work
optionA: Ask residents to run extra water so the flow pushes the liner into place more evenly
optionB: Set up bypass pumping sized for the expected flow for the installation and cure period
optionC: Seal every manhole upstream and let the sewage pond on the street surface overnight
optionD: Speed up the cure so bypass equipment is only needed for the first few minutes of work
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Rehabilitation Methods CIPP.
blueprintObjective: Collection System Components: Rehabilitation Methods CIPP

question: A pipe bursting job is planned on a street where a shallow gas main runs parallel and close to the sewer. Which precaution responds to the main risk of the method?
correctAnswer: Expose and monitor the nearby utilities, because the bursting head displaces soil outward as it advances
explanation: Bursting pushes the old pipe and surrounding soil outward. Nearby shallow utilities sit in that displacement zone, so they are exposed and watched during the pull.
options: Fill the sewer with water before bursting, because the added weight holds the soil in place around the pipe
Use the largest bursting head on hand, because a faster pull shortens the time the utilities are exposed
Skip the pre construction survey, because bursting follows the old pipe and cannot disturb other services
Expose and monitor the nearby utilities, because the bursting head displaces soil outward as it advances
optionA: Fill the sewer with water before bursting, because the added weight holds the soil in place around the pipe
optionB: Use the largest bursting head on hand, because a faster pull shortens the time the utilities are exposed
optionC: Skip the pre construction survey, because bursting follows the old pipe and cannot disturb other services

question: Two basins respond to the same storm. Basin A covers twice the area of Basin B and produces twice the RDII volume. Which extra step is needed before the utility can say which basin leaks more?
correctAnswer: Compare RDII per unit area or per unit of rainfall volume so the different basin sizes are accounted for
explanation: Raw RDII volumes grow with basin size and storm size. Dividing by area or rainfall volume puts both basins on the same footing before they are compared.
options: Compare RDII per unit area or per unit of rainfall volume so the different basin sizes are accounted for
Compare only the peak flows, because peak flow alone shows which basin has more defects per hectare
Compare the dry weather flows, because the RDII difference disappears once the storm response ends
Compare the manhole counts, because each manhole adds the same amount of RDII during a storm event
optionA: Compare RDII per unit area or per unit of rainfall volume so the different basin sizes are accounted for
optionB: Compare only the peak flows, because peak flow alone shows which basin has more defects per hectare
optionC: Compare the dry weather flows, because the RDII difference disappears once the storm response ends

question: A city rehabilitates its mainline sewers in a basin, but storm flows fall by only a small amount. Flow data and dye tests point to private property sources. Which next step fits the evidence?
correctAnswer: Extend the program to private laterals and foundation drains, where much of the remaining RDII enters
explanation: When mainline work barely moves storm flows, the remaining response is coming from somewhere else. The evidence points to private laterals and foundation drains.
options: Repeat the mainline lining a second time, because the first liner must have failed to seal the pipes
Declare the basin fixed, because mainline work removes the largest share of storm response in a basin
Extend the program to private laterals and foundation drains, where much of the remaining RDII enters
Stop monitoring the basin, because private property sources cannot be measured with field equipment

question: A CMOM annual review shows total overflow count falling, but the same four locations account for most of the remaining events. Which program adjustment does this pattern support?
correctAnswer: Target capacity and maintenance work at the repeat locations and track them as a separate performance measure
explanation: Falling totals show progress, but repeat locations show where the program still fails. CMOM review directs targeted work and separate tracking at those locations.
options: Spread the same budget evenly across the whole system so no single location receives more attention than another
Target capacity and maintenance work at the repeat locations and track them as a separate performance measure
Remove the four locations from the overflow records so the reported trend reflects the rest of the system only
Reduce inspections across the system, because the falling total count shows the program can ease its effort

question: A capital plan relies on CCTV grades recorded nine years ago for a reach that has since had two blockages and a repair. Which step protects the plan from acting on stale condition data?
correctAnswer: Re-inspect the reach and update its condition grade before committing rehabilitation funds to it
explanation: Condition changes over time, and blockages and repairs change it faster. Fresh inspection data keeps a capital plan from spending money on a grade that no longer applies.
options: Keep the old grade, because a condition grade stays valid until the pipe reaches its design life
Average the old grade with the grades of nearby reaches to smooth out the recent blockage history
Drop the reach from the plan, because a reach that has been repaired no longer needs condition data
Re-inspect the reach and update its condition grade before committing rehabilitation funds to it
optionA: Keep the old grade, because a condition grade stays valid until the pipe reaches its design life
optionB: Average the old grade with the grades of nearby reaches to smooth out the recent blockage history

question: A CCTV run shows several fractures clustered in one pipe length, with the wall starting to lose shape. A nearby length shows one hairline crack. Which coding decision reflects the difference?
correctAnswer: Code the clustered fractures at a higher structural grade, because wall support is being lost in that length
explanation: Structural grades rise as the wall loses support. Clustered fractures with shape loss are more severe than a single hairline crack with the wall still in place.
options: Code the clustered fractures at a higher structural grade, because wall support is being lost in that length
Code both lengths the same, because any visible crack receives the highest structural grade in the system
Code the hairline crack higher, because a single crack is harder for the camera operator to spot on video
Code neither length, because cracks and fractures count as maintenance items rather than structural defects in the system

question: A utility must choose which 50 of 400 manholes to seal this year. Inspection scores alone rank a dry hillside manhole equal to a riverside manhole with active infiltration stains. Which added data improves the choice?
correctAnswer: Flow and groundwater data showing where manhole infiltration adds the most flow to the system

The depth of each manhole below grade, showing which structures need the longest ladders

question: For one CIPP project the host pipe can still carry soil and traffic loads. For another, the host pipe is treated as fully deteriorated. Which design consequence follows?
correctAnswer: The fully deteriorated design needs a thicker liner, because the liner alone must carry the external loads
explanation: In a fully deteriorated design the host pipe is given no structural credit, so the liner must be thick enough to carry soil and traffic loads on its own.
options: Both designs use the same liner thickness, because the resin strength is the same in the two projects
The fully deteriorated design needs a thicker liner, because the liner alone must carry the external loads
The partially deteriorated design needs the thicker liner, because the host pipe adds load to the liner
Neither design considers external loads, because a cured liner is supported by the sewage flowing inside it
optionA: Both designs use the same liner thickness, because the resin strength is the same in the two projects
optionB: The fully deteriorated design needs a thicker liner, because the liner alone must carry the external loads
optionC: The partially deteriorated design needs the thicker liner, because the host pipe adds load to the liner

question: A project needs more capacity than the existing 250 mm sewer provides, and open cut work is ruled out by a busy arterial road. Which comparison correctly rules out slip lining for this job?
correctAnswer: Slip lining places a smaller pipe inside the host, so it cannot deliver the capacity increase the project needs
explanation: Slip lining always trades diameter for the new pipe wall and grout ring, so it cannot raise capacity above what the original host pipe provided.
options: Slip lining needs the host pipe removed first, so it cannot be used under a road that has to stay open to traffic
Slip lining cures a resin in place, so its chemical handling rules it out on any street that carries traffic
Slip lining expands the host pipe outward, so the road surface above the pipe would heave during the work
Slip lining places a smaller pipe inside the host, so it cannot deliver the capacity increase the project needs

question: A flow study meant to size an I&I program collected only two weeks of data, all in dry weather, before the meters were removed. Which weakness must the utility fix in the next study?
correctAnswer: Monitor through wet weather events as well, because dry weather data alone cannot show the rainfall response
explanation: An I&I program is sized on the rainfall response, so the study has to capture wet weather. Dry weather data alone describes only the base flow side of the problem.
options: Monitor through wet weather events as well, because dry weather data alone cannot show the rainfall response
Use fewer meters in the next study, because extra meters only repeat the data the first meter collects
Move all of the meters to the treatment plant, because basin level detail is not needed for an I&I program
Shorten the study to a single week, because longer studies add weather patterns that confuse the analysis
